name: Morocco (Darija)
description: Everything you need to get around Morocco — order food, find your way, handle money and emergencies — in the month before you go. Built to make you understood, and to help you understand what comes back.
grammarSpine: Verb-first, dropped subject: the verb prefix carries 'I/you/he', so a sentence is often just Verb + Object (bghit atay = 'want tea'). Adjectives follow the noun (atay skhun = 'tea hot').
Present tense = ka- + person: kan- (I), kat- (you), kay- (he/it). kanakol = I eat, katakol = you eat, kayakol = he eats.
Negation wraps the verb: ma ... sh. ma kanfhemsh = I don't understand.
Four power-words (fixed): bghit (I want), khessni (I need), 3andi (I have), kayn (there is).
Questions: front a question word (fin/shhal/ash/fuqash/kifash/shkun), or put 'wash' before a statement for yes/no.
Possession with dyal (l-flus dyali = my money); this/that = had / hadak.
Numbers — and the Moroccan money reality (dirham vs. rial).
